purpose: Every module under src/ that the running application does not reach, with the reason it does not and what would change that. scripts/lint-unreachable-modules.mjs fails when an unreachable module is ABSENT from this file. Unreachable is allowed here; unclassified is not. This register makes no claim that a listed module is right, only that its absence from the product is a decision somebody made and can be re-examined.
whyThisExists: docs/releases/RELEASE_NOTES_v0.6.6.md declares staged code publicly, under "Foundations added for a later release, not reachable in v0.6.6": implemented, tested, and not passed through by the running application, listed so the source is not mistaken for dead code. Nothing enforced that practice. A module staged deliberately in one release and forgotten in the next leave the same tree behind, and a superseded module is indistinguishable from one waiting to be wired. The register is where those cases are told apart.
method: Breadth-first closure from the module scripts index.html loads, over static value imports, static type-only imports, dynamic import() with a literal specifier, and new Worker(new URL(...)). Dynamic edges are counted, which is why src/lazyChunks.ts is not a leaf: it holds this repository's dynamic import() literals and most lazy features hang off it. Type-only edges are counted too, so a module reached only by an erased import is NOT listed here; that widening keeps the register about modules nothing in the product refers to at all. It is a file-level graph, so it cannot see an unused export, and reachable is not executed.

measuredAt.note: The runtime-only figure drops type-only edges and is recorded for context. It is larger because 88 modules are reached from production solely through an `import type`, which is erased at build time. The register is keyed on the wider graph.
measuredAt.basis: The pre-tag tree this measurement was taken on. The tagged commit differs, because recording a measurement changes the tree; the release workflow records the tag.

statuses.staged: Implemented and tested, deliberately not wired, intended to be reached later. The graduation gate names the wiring that would do it.
statuses.validation-only: Produces or checks evidence about the product. It runs in tests, studies and gate scripts and must stay out of the application graph; becoming reachable would be the defect.
statuses.reference-only: Consumed by something outside the application entry graph, such as the build configuration or a lint, rather than by the running application.
statuses.orphan: Superseded or abandoned. Nothing outside its own test consumes it and nothing is expected to. The graduation gate names the removal or the replacement it lost to.

reviewDates: Reported by the lint when they pass, never enforced. A gate that turns red on a date with no change to the tree teaches people to edit the date rather than the code.

modules.why: Named in the v0.6.6 release notes as "tie-point rigid registration with control-network validation". Horn absolute orientation over labelled correspondences; no UI collects the correspondences.

modules.why: Named in the v0.6.6 release notes as "a local out-of-core read planner", listed under "Foundations added for a later release, not reachable in v0.6.6". The claim that local files use the whole-file path is no longer true: src/app/openScan.ts now routes a large uncompressed LAS through openLocalHeavyLas.ts and src/io/heavy/localOocBuild.ts, a separate heavy-LAS bridge that peeks the header and streams tiles instead of materialising one ArrayBuffer. That bridge superseded the LAS half of the role this planner was staged for. A large chunked LAZ now takes the same bridge: openScan.ts routes it through openLocalHeavyLas.ts, which sniffs the header format and, for a LAZ with a usable chunk table, builds tiles through src/io/heavy/localOocBuild.ts and buildTileStoreFromLaz; a LAZ without a usable chunk table is refused rather than read whole. The planner itself remains unreachable: only its own test imports planOutOfCore.
modules.graduation: Either this becomes the shared LAS-plus-future-LAZ read planner the open path consults before choosing a reader, or, if the heavy-LAS bridge covers the need and the LAZ builder lands separately, it is removed. Decide when the chunked-LAZ path is designed.

modules.why: The Continuity Field's display-epoch core. The subsystem ships with every capability off, so the renderer does not yet open an epoch or ask whether one is still valid, and nothing constructs a DisplayState.
modules.graduation: A capability turns on and the render loop drives the epoch, so a reused frame is gated on advanceEpoch rather than redrawn unconditionally.

modules.why: Sun-direction shading over the elevation ramp. src/render/inspectionPresets.ts states the matching fact from the other side: the preset it belongs to has "no runtime setter behind" it and "there is no live hillshade renderer to switch".
modules.graduation: A hillshade colour mode exists in colorModes and the Viewer can switch it on.

modules.why: Maps the renderer's existing frame-time pressure onto a continuity tier. No tier is selected and every capability is off, so nothing asks.
modules.graduation: The render loop holds a current tier and asks this each decision, feeding the same smoothed frame time the scheduler already reacts to rather than sampling its own.

modules.why: Chooses how far the field may go on a given backend and what it falls back to. Every capability is off, so no tier is ever selected.
modules.graduation: The renderer detects what a backend supports, asks for a tier and applies its capabilities, falling to source rendering rather than failing when none can be carried.

modules.why: Schedules which temporal phase a parked frame contributes and when the sweep is complete. No frame accumulates, so nothing asks it.
modules.graduation: Accumulation turns on and the render loop drives the sweep from this state, stopping when it reports converged. The EDL repaint must move with it: edlMotionGate runs EDL once the moment motion stops, which is the first frame of the sweep, so it would shade an image that is one phase complete and never run again. It has to fire on converged instead of on parked.

modules.why: Decides whether a new sample replaces, joins or loses to the accumulation history at a pixel. No history buffers exist, so no sample is ever tested against one.
modules.graduation: The accumulation pass keeps history colour, depth and support, and applies this decision per sample, with the depth tolerance measured against near geometry and distant terrain.

modules.why: Decides where the renderer stops substituting reconstruction and shows measured evidence. Nothing reconstructs, so there is nothing to reveal and no lens is opened.
modules.graduation: Reconstruction runs and the lens suppresses it under the cursor, reachable from Inspect, Measure or Probe, with picking unchanged whether it is open or shut.

modules.why: Sizes the accumulation history and picks its texture formats. No history is allocated, so nothing asks what it would cost.
modules.graduation: The accumulation pass allocates history at these formats, declines above the ceiling and leaves source rendering in place, and releases the textures when the device pixel ratio changes rather than keeping an oversized one.

modules.why: Decides whether a background pixel may borrow a depth from its cardinal neighbours. No reconstruction pass runs, so no pixel is ever offered.
modules.graduation: The reconstruction pass runs over unsupported pixels and marks what it writes as reconstructed, with the evidence lens able to show those pixels apart from measured ones. Before it is enabled, the six raster exporters must be settled: BaseExportMode captures the live on-screen canvas, so a height, depth or normal raster would carry invented geometry with nothing in FigureStampContext recording it. Either the field is off for a capture, or the stamp declares reconstruction.

modules.why: Decides how many temporal phases a moving frame draws and how much wider each drawn point must be. No frame draws a subset today, so nothing asks.
modules.graduation: A measurement on a real device shows a phase subset buys frame time that the existing motion reductions have not already taken, and the render loop draws that subset.

modules.why: Decides whether a resident streaming node is in front of the camera, from the node's own bounds. Every point mesh, static or streamed, is built by the Viewer's shared builder, which sets frustumCulled = false; for a streamed node that means one held warm in the cache is submitted for drawing whether or not the camera contains it. The baseline in docs/validation/streaming-cull-baseline.json measures what that costs on stored cameras: a zoomed view draws 24 of 84 resident nodes and a narrow one 12 of 84. Pure arithmetic with no three.js, so the decision is testable without a renderer. Only its tests and that benchmark import it.
modules.graduation: The streaming renderer sets each node mesh's visibility from cullResidentNodes behind a development flag, and a run on a real device shows the submitted-node count falling with no popping and no node hidden while visible. The flag decides the default, not this module: the arithmetic is settled, the tradeoff is a measurement this runtime cannot take. Residency must stay independent, so a culled node is skipped by the draw and never evicted.

modules.why: Its own header states the position: the P8 fetch/decode/upload separation is evidence-gated, so this is "the policy math only ... NOT wired into the live scheduler", and wiring waits on device profiling that shows the P7 upload queue did not already resolve the stalls.
modules.graduation: On-device profiling shows remaining value and the scheduler adopts these limits.

modules.why: It maps a device tier onto a full bundle of streaming-session defaults: quality preset, EDL default and fade-in. The direct calls did not settle its question, they left its value unrealised. src/main.ts hardcodes the initial streamingQuality to 'balanced' and never derives it from deviceCapsValue.tier; streamingBudgets(quality, isMobile) is called with that fixed quality. So no path yet turns a device tier into these session defaults as a whole. tierAdaptation.ts, itself staged, is written to layer runtime FPS stepping on top of this bundle, which marks it as intended future work rather than a superseded module. Wiring it would edit src/main.ts, held off here because concurrent work owns that file.
modules.graduation: The attach path in src/main.ts derives its initial streaming quality, EDL and fade-in defaults from streamingProfileForTier(deviceCapsValue.tier, isPhone()) instead of the hardcoded 'balanced'.

modules.why: Counts drawn pixels by whether they were measured, carried over or invented. No pass records support per pixel, so there is nothing to count.
modules.graduation: The renderer tracks support provenance per pixel and a regression test fails a frame whose reconstructed share passes the ceiling, with that ceiling set from real scenes at several densities.

modules.why: Assigns each point a temporal phase for the accumulation capability. That capability is off, so no frame draws a subset and nothing asks a point which phase it is in.
modules.graduation: Temporal accumulation turns on and the size graph folds the phase in as its own node, independent of the fade dither, which endNodeDissolve drops once a node settles.

modules.why: Runtime FPS-driven tier stepping with hysteresis, written to layer on top of streamingProfile. Nothing feeds it FPS samples.
modules.graduation: The render loop feeds FPS samples in and applies the tier it returns.

modules.why: The canonical descriptor of the delivered DTM method plus a SHA-256 method digest, for the external-validation and export-provenance paths: a stamped digest can be compared against a fresh resolve to prove the delivered method has not drifted. The scoped-evidence resolver and the E5 reduce path will read it, but neither construction is wired into the application graph yet, so only its test imports it.
modules.graduation: Export provenance stamps dtmMethodDigest into the DTM evidence context, or the E5 reduce path resolves the descriptor to verify the candidate method, at which point the application graph reaches it. Before this graduates, the method-identity contract must be settled: the header says per-dataset fields are context and do NOT feed dtmMethodDigest, while methodBehaviourFields includes horizontalUnitToMetres and verticalUnitToMetres and a test requires 1 -> 0.3048 to change the digest. Either the unit scales are run context and leave the digest, or the digest is a fully parameterised method identity and the header says so. A digest whose own module disagrees about what it identifies cannot support a published reproducibility claim.
